name: SNDK AI Fundamental Valuation
rationale: Sandisk Corporation (SNDK) is a primary core holding in the Data Infra / Storage pillar. TTM revenue surged to $20.25B with GAAP net income of $11.43B (56.46% net margin). 5-year DCF yields a fair value of $1,720.21 (+9.8% upside vs $1,566.70 market price). Reverse DCF indicates the market is pricing in a 19.14% 5-year CAGR, well within achievable enterprise flash growth rates. Recommendation: MAINTAIN (Core Holding). Accumulate on dips <$1,290, trim Tier 1 at $1,720.21.

bear.rationale: Memory downcycle hits as hyperscalers pause capex and competitor NAND capacity floods market. Revenue growth decelerates sharply to 8% CAGR over 5 years. Severe ASP erosion compresses net margins to 25% (down from 56% peak). Multiple compresses to 14x trough hardware multiple. Quality multiplier 0.9 reflects cyclical vulnerability and commodity memory risk.
risks: Aggressive NAND wafer fab expansion by competitors (Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron) creates severe supply glut
Enterprise AI SSD adoption peaks early, leading to inventory destocking

base.rationale: AI datacenter high-capacity QLC SSD and PCIe Gen5 flash demand sustains solid 16% 5-year CAGR after initial +370% post-spinoff baseline ramp. Net margins normalize from hyper-peak 56% down to a highly profitable steady-state 38% as ASPs stabilize. Exit P/E of 20x reflects premium semiconductor storage franchise. Quality multiplier 1.05 reflects proprietary BiCS NAND architecture and long-term enterprise OEM design wins.
risks: Normalization of AI infrastructure memory intensity faster than expected
Cyclical ASP softening during mid-cycle transition

bull.rationale: Sustained high-density AI storage supercycle (64TB-128TB enterprise SSDs replacing HDDs in AI training & inference clusters). 24% revenue CAGR drives scale to $59B+ by Year 5. High-margin custom enterprise firmware and tight supply preserve 48% net margins. Multiple re-rates to 26x semiconductor growth multiple. Quality multiplier 1.15 reflects mission-critical datacenter lock-in and share repurchases.
risks: Alternative memory architectures (HBM, CXL memory pooling) cannibalize flash storage tier
Export controls on advanced high-layer 3D NAND equipment and components
